subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Gallium Nitride: The New Power Player
description: A short lesson to help you apply Gallium Nitride: The New Power Player.

hook.text: Silicon struggles above 200°C and at high voltages. Gallium nitride doesn't flinch.

buildup.text: GaN has a wider band gap (3.4 eV vs 1.1 eV). It handles higher voltages and temperatures.

discovery.text: GaN transistors switch faster with lower losses — ideal for power converters.

twist.text: Your fast phone charger is probably GaN. It's half the size of an old silicon charger.

climax.text: GaN is also used in 5G base stations, electric vehicle inverters, and radar systems.

punchline.text: When silicon can't take the heat, gallium nitride steps in.

quiz.question: Why is GaN better than silicon for high-power applications?
options: It is cheaper to produce than silicon
Its wider band gap allows higher voltages, temperatures, and faster switching
It conducts heat better than any other semiconductor
